name: SMS, calendar and call log
plain: A site cannot send or read SMS, read the calendar, or see call history.
meaning: sms: and tel: links only open the user's own app. Calendars arrive as .ics downloads or OAuth sign in.

web.api: (none); closest proxy: <a href='sms:...'>, Contact Picker, downloaded .ics

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: A site cannot send or read SMS, read the calendar, or see call history.

limits.headline: Can't send or see your text messages, calendar or call history from a website
limits.user_action: You tap an sms: link, tel: link, or a calendar file or sign in button
can: Open your own messaging or phone app with a number or message filled in
Offer an .ics calendar file for you to open
Connect to your calendar if you sign in with an approved account
cannot: Send a text message by itself
See your calendar without a sign in you approve

story.what_it_is: A website cannot send or read your texts, read your calendar or see your call history.

marketing.name: Contact Picker API
marketing.pitch: The closest tool: you pick contacts to share one at a time, and the site sees only your pick.

story.for_you: A site cannot read your messages, calendar or calls. If it needs a contact, you pick one yourself. It is a wall that protects your private data.
story.for_makers: Makers who want these features must ask you to share them one at a time, use a link or an email, or build a native app. This blocks mass data grabs. They rely on forms and sharing instead.

use_cases.example: A web chat wanted to read your texts to find friends. It asks you to pick contacts or import a file instead.
A scheduling site wanted to read your calendar. It uses a link you paste or a calendar sign in that you approve.
A social site wanted your call history to suggest friends. It asks you to pick contacts one by one.
A site wanted to read SMS login codes. It uses a one time code API that reads one code with your approval.
A store wanted to send an order text from your phone. It sends texts from its server instead.
A health site wanted calendar entries to book a visit. It offers a file you add to your calendar.
A travel site wanted to put the trip on your calendar. It offers a calendar file to download.
